findings.title: JWT client credentials fail with this provider
findings.body: When the authz-client is used without another crypto provider on the classpath, service discovery selects this provider, but `getSignature()` always throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. The authz-client documents support for JWT credentials, whose client assertions need a signing implementation; that flow therefore fails instead of obtaining a token. The other unsupported crypto operations can similarly break callers that use the selected provider.

findings.title: ECDSA conversion silently accepts oversized signatures
findings.body: This method copies only the first `signLength` bytes and never checks that the input has exactly that length. When used to convert an untrusted JOSE ECDSA signature for verification, a signature with arbitrary trailing bytes is converted as though those bytes were absent, so malformed, non-canonical signatures can verify as the valid prefix. Inputs shorter than the expected length instead throw `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`. Reject any input whose length differs from `signLength`.

findings.title: Equal provider orders make FIPS selection depend on discovery order
findings.body: The default, Elytron, and FIPS providers all return order `200`, so when more than one is visible the sort does not establish a preference; the selected implementation depends on service-resource discovery order. In particular, a classpath containing both the default and FIPS providers can silently select the default provider, undermining the configured FIPS crypto implementation. Assign distinct priorities or reject ambiguous top-ranked providers.

findings.title: Adding an abstract method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: `CryptoProvider` is a service-provider interface, and adding an abstract `order()` method breaks implementations compiled against the previous interface. Such providers either fail to compile when rebuilt or throw `AbstractMethodError` when `CryptoIntegration` invokes `order()` during provider sorting, preventing startup. Make the method backward-compatible with a default implementation or otherwise preserve compatibility.
